items.readable_text:
Content:
A unit vector is a vector whose magnitude is equal to [MATH: 1.]

Content:
Given any vector [MATH: \mathbf a], we can create a unit vector [MATH: \mathbf u] by dividing [MATH: \mathbf a] by its magnitude [MATH: |\, \mathbf{a} \,|,] as follows:
[MATH: \mathbf{u} = \dfrac{ \mathbf{a} }{ |\,\mathbf{a}\,| }]

Content:
For example, if [MATH: |\,\mathbf{a}\,|=2,] then the unit vector is
[MATH: \mathbf{u} = \dfrac{\mathbf{a}}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2} \mathbf{a}.]

items.title: Finding a Unit Vector Parallel to a Vector Sum

sections.normalized_html: The vector [MATH: \mathbf{a}] is directed horizontally to the right and has magnitude [MATH: 10,] while the vector [MATH: \mathbf{b}] is directed vertically down and has magnitude [MATH: 20.] Find a unit vector that is parallel to [MATH: \mathbf{a+b}.]
sections.readable_text: The vector [MATH: \mathbf{a}] is directed horizontally to the right and has magnitude [MATH: 10,] while the vector [MATH: \mathbf{b}] is directed vertically down and has magnitude [MATH: 20.] Find a unit vector that is parallel to [MATH: \mathbf{a+b}.]

sections.normalized_html:
First, we have to find [MATH: \mathbf{a+b}.] According to the triangle law of addition, the resultant [MATH: \mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b}] goes from the tail of [MATH: \mathbf{a}] to the head of [MATH: \mathbf{b}\mathbin{:}]

To find the unit vector corresponding to [MATH: \mathbf{a+b},] we have to divide by the magnitude: [MATH: u|= (a + b)/(|a + b|)]

To find the magnitude, first notice that we obtain a right triangle. So, we can use the Pythagorean theorem: [MATH: |a + b|^{2}|=|a|^{2} +|b|^{2}; = 10^{2} + 20^{2}; = 100 + 400; = 500]

Therefore, the magnitude is [MATH: |\mathbf{a+b}|=\sqrt{500}=10\sqrt{5},] and the corresponding unit vector is [MATH: u|= (a + b)/(|a + b|); = (1)/(10sqrt(5))(a + b).]

[MATH: |\mathbf{a+b}|=\sqrt{500}=10\sqrt{5},]
